transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-07-27
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~49 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Liam O'Rourke (Redwood SE), Anita Patel (Crestline Head of AI), Marcus Lee (Infra Lead), Sofia Ruiz (Product), Daniel Gomez (Finance)

Summary:
Quick QBR-style health check focused on service fitness (latency/cost), upcoming model rollout (canary + rollout phasing), and budget/fiscal guardrails. Customer asked for concrete cost levers and a short stress-run to validate p95/p99 for their checkout conversational assistant. Agreed next steps and owners.

Topics:
- current usage patterns & recent spike analysis
- SLA and SLO alignment; p95 vs p99 expectations
- batching / KV cache opportunities to reduce unit costs
- dedicated vs hosted tradeoffs for peak 2x traffic days
- compliance packet & VPC onboarding checklist

00:00 Maya Chen: hey everyone, thanks for joining, i'll do a 2 minute kickoff, then Liam will go into the performance bits.
00:14 Anita Patel: thanks, yeah we've got limited time, wanted to focus on last month's surge and cost delta, also the model roll.
00:30 Liam O'Rourke: cool, quick agenda—health snapshot, latency and errors, economic levers, proposed canary plan.
00:45 Marcus Lee: real quick—during the spike we saw average seq length jump to ~380 tokens on checkout prompts, that hit our budget pretty hard.
01:05 Maya Chen: ok, that's useful, thanks. the spike also aligns with a higher KV miss rate we observed on our end — K-V cash hit was like 22% during peak, so fewer cache savings.
01:28 Sofia Ruiz: sorry was that K-V cash or K-V cache? audio glitch —
01:34 Liam O'Rourke: KV cache, yeah. there's sometimes transcription oddness in our logs, but it's cache miss.
01:50 Daniel Gomez: from finance view the burn was 37% above forecast for that week, we need predictable capex for q3.
02:10 Maya Chen: understood — two buckets of work: quick wins (batching, prefix caching) and medium runway (dedicated capacity or reserved). we'll show numbers.
02:36 Liam O'Rourke: i'll jump into the perf numbers — so p50 is fine, p95 moved from 210ms to 380ms in peak, p99 up to 1.2s. those p99s usually map to KV cache refill and shorter batch sizes.
03:05 Marcus Lee: we currently batch at client side with size 8, but burst windows make us send single-rpc calls often, because the UX wants instant answers.
03:30 Anita Patel: that's the problem—we can't sacrifice perceived latency at checkout, even 200ms matters. so we need solutions that maintain p95 tight while reducing cost.
03:50 Liam O'Rourke: two levers—intelligent batching on the server side with bounded latency SLOs, and model variant routing; fallback to a cheaper quantized variant for non-critical routes.
04:10 Maya Chen: also prefix-level KV caching for repetitive prompts in the checkout flow — that'll hit their reuse patterns.
04:30 Sofia Ruiz: how feasible is a quantized variant with our existing models, will that affect quality?
04:45 Liam O'Rourke: small drop in rouge/bleu-style metrics for some generative tasks, but for structured assistant responses we tested it's within tolerance. we'd run quick evals on your prompts.
05:05 Anita Patel: can you quantify cost reduction? we need a slide we can take to finance.
05:18 Maya Chen: yes — rough ballpark: batching + prefix cache could reduce token compute by 18–28% depending on cache hit; adding quantized routing another 12% on eligible traffic. we'll send a per-route spreadsheet.
05:45 Daniel Gomez: put that in numbers: example week X -> how much $ saved.
05:52 Maya Chen: will do, note: these are model-and-traffic dependent.
06:10 Liam O'Rourke: on the dedicated vs hosted question—if you need guaranteed headroom for sale days, dedicated gives you reserved throughput but costs baseline more. hosted with reserved bursts is cheaper but less isolated.
06:40 Marcus Lee: does Redwood offer burst-only options so we don't pay for idle reserved capacity?
06:50 Maya Chen: yes we have burst capacity and autoscale policies, plus can pair reserved commit + burst buffer. we'll include a cost scenario comparing three configs.
07:05 Anita Patel: security/compliance check — we need to share SOC2 docs and confirm VPC onboarding lead times.
07:18 Liam O'Rourke: we can share SOC2 packet, our console supports customer-managed VPC routes, and for on-prem we have an install guide. expect 2–4 week lead for full VPC onboarding depending on approvals.
07:42 Sofia Ruiz: would that include KMS integration for encryption at rest?
07:48 Maya Chen: yes, KMS/HSM options available; we'll add the integration checklist.
08:00 Daniel Gomez: thinking ahead for q4 budget ask—if we go dedicated any time this quarter, when's the earliest we can lock?
08:12 Maya Chen: earliest lock would be mid-August for a Sep commit, assuming agreement and payment terms—timeline depends on procurement cycle.
08:30 Liam O'Rourke: back to ops—i'd like to propose a quick 48-hour stress run on your real payload to capture p95/p99 under realistic burst patterns. can we get access to replay logs?
08:45 Marcus Lee: yes we can provide sanitized replay logs, might take a day to scrub.
09:00 Anita Patel: also want a canary plan for the model roll — how many users, metrics to watch, rollback criteria.
09:15 Liam O'Rourke: proposed canary: 5% traffic for first 48 hours, watch latency, error rate, and quality evals on a small prompt set. rollback if p99 increases >30% or quality degrades >5% on eval set.
09:40 Sofia Ruiz: that rollback criteria seems ok to product — we just need clear owners.
10:00 Maya Chen: owner map—Redwood will monitor infra metrics, Crestline owns product-level metrics and sign-off.
10:12 Daniel Gomez: from finance, we want an upfront estimate of monthly runrate delta before canary.
10:25 Maya Chen: we'll put that in the cost spreadsheet.

10:40 Transcript noise / side chatter: a couple short cross-talks during the spike discussion, some mis-heard model names (we heard 'Redwood Dedicat' in transcript).

11:00 Wrap-up and explicit next steps:
- Maya to email per-route cost sheet and scenario compare (reserved/dedicated/hosted+burst).
- Liam to schedule the 48h stress run and request replay logs from Marcus.
- Anita to share SOC2 recipients and compliance questions.
- All to align on pilot kickoff week of 2026-08-10.

Questions raised (short list):
- What is expected lead time for VPC onboarding? (answered: 2–4 weeks typical)
- How much can quantized routing impact quality on assistant prompts? (answered: small impact, recommend evals)
- Can burst-only capacity avoid reserved commit? (answered: yes with limits, will propose scenarios)

Closing remarks:
Maya Chen: thanks everyone — we'll run the stress tests, get you the numbers early next week, and reconvene once you have SOC2 recipients.
Anita Patel: appreciate the focus, looking forward to the cost sheet.

End of meeting.
